title: Community Health Worker (CHW) Certificate
description: This certificate will equip the learners with the essential skills and knowledge required to support community health initiatives and promote public well-being.
longDescription: This programme prepares learners to assist in implementing public health policies, coordinate health resources, and collaborate with healthcare professionals. It aims to build competence in delivering basic health interventions and empowering communities towards healthier lifestyles. It will help them understand key concepts in health education, disease prevention, and health promotion strategies within communities. Learners will develop the ability to apply basic healthcare practices, conduct outreach programs, and support vulnerable populations. They will also demonstrate effective communication, cultural sensitivity, and advocacy skills to enhance community health outcomes. The course will commence in the first week of November.
courseDetails: Explain the role and responsibilities of a community health worker. Understand the structure of community health programs. Apply basic public health principles in community settings. Demonstrate techniques for identifying community health needs. Recognize the importance of health promotion in public health. Maintain professionalism in community health practice. Understand the principles of health promotion and education. Apply strategies to prevent common community health issues. Demonstrate effective use of educational tools and materials. Identify high-risk groups within a community. Collaborate with health teams to implement preventive programs. Evaluate the impact of health promotion campaigns. Understand the importance of communication in community health. Apply effective communication techniques with diverse groups. Demonstrate cultural sensitivity in health interventions. Recognize barriers to communication in different populations. Promote community participation in health programs. Maintain ethical and respectful interactions with all community members. Understand basic healthcare practices for community health workers. Apply first aid techniques for minor injuries and emergencies. Demonstrate safe handling of medical supplies and equipment. Recognize symptoms that require medical referral. Support families with basic hygiene and nutrition guidance. Maintain records of community health visits and interventions. The Community Health Worker Certificate equips learners with the skills to promote health, provide basic care, and connect communities with essential health and social services. The program focuses on health education, disease prevention, cultural competence, advocacy, and effective communication. Learners will understand community health needs, apply strategies to support vulnerable populations, and demonstrate professionalism in outreach and care delivery. By the end of the course, graduates will be prepared to assist healthcare systems in improving access, quality, and outcomes of care at the community level. After the successful completion of this course, you will be able to: Unit 1: Introduction to Community Health Work Learning Outcomes: Unit 2: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Unit 3: Communication and Cultural Sensitivity Unit 4: Basic Healthcare Support and First Aid

modules.title: Community Health Worker
modules.summary: The Community Health Worker Certificate equips learners with the knowledge and skills to support individuals, families, and communities in accessing healthcare services and improving overall well-being. The program emphasizes health promotion, disease prevention, and advocacy within diverse populations. Students gain expertise in communication, cultural competence, and outreach strategies. Training includes assessing community health needs, providing basic health education, and connecting people to appropriate resources. Practical experience enhances the ability to build trust and address social determinants of health. Graduates are prepared to work in clinics, non-profits, government programs, and community organizations.
